notes: Partition verified: 29 source and 39 target ids each used once across 26 units.

`לֹא` takes the determiner *no* recast onto the subject nominal (rule 15); the verb keeps the presentative *There*, its auxiliary and the modal frame *be able to*, which is an auxiliary periphrasis of a written verb rather than rule 20's wholly supplied lexical verb.
`פַּחְדְּכֶם וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם` is aligned in the Hebrew's own order (`פַּחַד` → *fear*, `מוֹרָא` → *dread*); the reverse mapping was the competing reading and would not move any edge.

`בָהּ` is split here — *upon* to the stranded preposition, the resumptive suffix `unrepresented` under rule 22 — because the relative alone is written for the antecedent, unlike the fused *therein* of DEU.11.31.
